evidence.quote: Fabrication of the Perovskite Hybrid Solar Cells (Pero-HSCs) : The pero-HSCs were fabricated in the device with a confi guration of ITO/ PEDOT:PSS/CH 3 NH 3 PbI 3x Cl x /PC 61 BM/Al, where ITO is indium tin oxide, CH 3 NH 3 PbI 3x Cl x is perovskite materials, and Al is Aluminum. Approximately 35 nm of PEDOT:PSS was spin-coated on precleaned ITO glass substrates followed by thermal annealing at 150 ° C for 10 min. The perovskite fi lms were spin-coated on top of ITO/PEDOT:PSS from perovskite precursor solution in the glove box with nitrogen atmosphere. The perovskite thin fi lms were processed by two-step procedures.

unresolved_notes: The source does not establish that the Figure 8a J-V device, Figure 8b IPCE device, and Figure 8c hysteresis device are the same physical cell; they are therefore kept as separate individual-device records.

Figure 8c reports only the efficiency difference between forward and reversed directions, not a direction-specific efficiency or other direction-specific outcome. The comparative result is retained in one observation with scan direction not reported rather than duplicated into unsupported forward and reverse observations.

The source establishes that pero-HSCs charged flexible solid-state supercapacitors in the integrated system, but it does not identify a particular photovoltaic specimen or report a photovoltaic-device metric for that charging experiment. The discharge voltage, current density, and time are supercapacitor/system outcomes and are not extracted as photovoltaic performance observations.
The stated high vacuum is preserved verbatim as “2 × 10 6 mbar”; no missing negative exponent was inferred.
The source reports the second-procedure spin time only as “tuned from 20 s”; no final spin time was inferred.
The source does not explicitly report the device polarity or the electrical roles of PEDOT:PSS and PC61BM, so those classifications remain not reported.

The precursor sentence reports CH3NH3I and PbCl2 together with a molar ratio of 3:1. Following the explicitly coordinated scope, the same source-reported ratio is retained as separate item-specific values; no additional stoichiometric interpretation is inferred.

No photovoltaic population statistic or photovoltaic aging or operational-stability outcome is reported. The supplied cycling and storage stability results concern solid-state supercapacitors, not photovoltaic devices.

The self-powered-electronics passages report a system-level integration of flexible solid-state supercapacitors with pero-HSCs through two copper wires and a supercapacitor discharge from 0.75 V to 0 V at 1 A g -1 for about 45 s under/after white-light charging. They do not identify one individual photovoltaic device, and the reported discharge outcomes belong to the supercapacitor/integrated system rather than to an explicitly linked individual PV device.
